summary: find searches a folder and every folder inside it for files that match rules you give it, like a name pattern or a type.
notes: The first argument is where to start. . means the current folder, so find . searches everything below where you are.
-type d lists folders and -type f lists files. You can combine rules: find . -type f -name "*.txt".
In -exec wc -l {} \; the {} is replaced by each file name, and \; marks the end of the command.
pitfall: find . -name *.py without quotes lets the shell expand *.py first. In cs it finds only ./hello.py and misses ./project/src/main.py. Always quote the pattern: find . -name "*.py".
